name: FSI German Basic Course
what: Public-domain drill course: 24 units, student-text PDFs, tape MP3s
use: Free US-government course: a book (PDF) and audio. Its pattern drills are close to this app’s drills.
note: Whole course also as one ZIP (FSI-German-Basic.zip) on the same page. Live Lingua hosts a copy but its course list was not navigable in the check.

useByStage.1: After Nicos Weg: open Unit 1 (the Volume 1 PDF and the Unit 1 audio files). Play the dialogue, pause after each line and say it out loud. Then do the drills: say the answer before the speaker does. Units 1–4 over weeks 1–4.
useByStage.2: One unit a week: dialogue first, then say every drill answer before the speaker does.
useByStage.3: Keep one unit a week; shadow the dialogue speaker (speak along half a second behind).

tip: The course is from the 1960s, so some words are old-fashioned, but the grammar drills are excellent. The page also offers the whole course as one ZIP file.

name: Nicos Weg (Deutsche Welle)
what: Free video course A1–B1 with transcripts and exercises
use: Free video course that follows Nico, who has just arrived in Germany. One episode a day.
note: learngerman.dw.com is blocked by this session's egress proxy (CONNECT 403), so the page could not be loaded. URL confirmed verbatim via the podcast directory listing for the DW Nicos Weg A1 feed. A1 in stage 1, A2 in stage 2, B1 in stage 3.

useByStage.1: Start at A1, lesson 1 (“Hallo!”). Watch the episode, then watch it again with the German subtitles on and repeat each line out loud. Do the short exercises under the video. One lesson a day.
useByStage.2: Move on to the A2 episodes: watch once without subtitles, then again with them, repeating the lines you missed.
useByStage.3: B1 episodes: watch without subtitles; check yourself with the transcript afterwards.

tip: On the page choose A1, then lesson 1 “Hallo!”. Free; no account needed to watch.

name: DW placement test
what: Free online placement test, A1–C1, instant level
use: Free online level test. Take it at the end of week 12 and again at month 6.
note: Host blocked by the egress proxy. Path confirmed from a Hochschule Darmstadt handout that gives https://learngerman.dw.com/de/placementDashboard; the /en/ form is the English UI of the same page. If it 404s, use the /de/ form.

name: Easy German (YouTube)
what: Street interviews and Super Easy German, dual subtitles
use: Street interviews with Germans. Use the “Super Easy German” videos with subtitles for input, and one ordinary interview without subtitles for gisting.
note: Playlists are sorted by level on the channel; start with the A1/A2 playlist. Natural-speed interviews are a stage-3 gisting source, not a stage-1 one.
tip: The channel sorts videos into playlists by level; start with the beginner playlist.

name: Easy German site and podcast
what: Podcast, level guide, paid interactive transcripts and community
use: The Easy German podcast: play one episode and note the topics.
note: Podcast page: https://www.easygerman.org/podcast (loaded). Transcripts are members-only; the videos on YouTube carry subtitles for free.
tip: Transcripts need a paid membership; the audio is free.

name: Nachrichtenleicht (Deutschlandfunk)
what: Weekly news in simple German, text plus 1-minute audio
use: News in simple German, with audio. Read two short articles; then play the audio of one without the text and note who, what and where.
note: Also as a podcast feed (Spotify/Apple/RSS) and in the Deutschlandfunk app; the site has a Wörter-Buch glossary.
tip: Also available as a podcast.

name: Slow German podcast
what: Slow, clear podcast on German life with read-along texts
use: Podcast spoken slowly by one speaker. Play 2 minutes, then speak along with her without the text, then with the text.
note: Content is pitched at B1+, so in stage 1 use it for rhythm and sounds only, not for comprehension; the free episodes and texts suffice. Premium area is optional.
tip: Aimed at intermediate learners, so it is too hard before week 9.

name: Tagesschau in 100 Sekunden
what: ARD's 100-second national news video, updated hourly
use: The day’s news in 100 seconds. Play it once without text and write down the topics, numbers and names you caught.
note: tagesschau.de is blocked by this session's egress proxy (CONNECT 403). URL confirmed verbatim from third-party scripts that embed the clip. Also available as a video podcast in any podcast app.
tip: Real news at full speed: aim for the topics, not the words.

name: ARD Audiothek
what: Public-broadcaster podcasts and radio features, no transcripts
use: German public-radio features and podcasts. Pick one short piece a week and note the topic and the speakers.
note: Host blocked by this session's egress proxy; URL is the broadcaster's standard domain. Also an app on iOS/Android.

name: Play SRF (Swiss broadcaster)
what: Swiss public TV on demand: Tagesschau, Schweiz aktuell
use: Swiss TV. From month 10, one Swiss news clip a week to get used to Swiss-accented German.
note: Month 10+ only, per the doctrine; some content is geo-restricted outside Switzerland. SRF news articles are at https://www.srf.ch/ (loaded).
tip: Some videos only play inside Switzerland.

name: Goethe B1 practice exam
what: Two free B1 model exams: PDFs, listening audio, word list
use: The official free B1 practice papers with answers and audio. In week 11 try one reading task to see the level; from month 4 do one full part a month under exam timing.
note: Downloads on the page: Prüfungstraining 1 and 2 (PDF with answer keys, Hören audio), Wortliste B1, Sprechen example video. Use the Erwachsene (adult) set.

name: telc B1 practice exam
what: Official telc B1 mock exam with audio, free ZIP
use: The other accepted B1 exam. From month 6 do its practice test once under timing and compare with your Goethe scores before choosing which exam to book.
note: Direct download named on the page: https://www.telc.net/fileadmin/user_upload/mock_exams/Deutsch/telc_deutsch_b1.zip (test + audio).

name: dict.cc dictionary
what: German–English dictionary with gender, plural, audio
use: Look up any word you meet. Write every noun down with der/die/das and its plural (der Tisch, die Tische), never as a bare word.
tip: Many entries have a speaker icon so you can hear the word.

name: LEO German–English
what: Dictionary with conjugation and declension tables, forums
use: Second dictionary. Its tables show every form of a verb or noun when you are unsure of an ending.

name: DWDS corpus dictionary
what: Academic dictionary with corpus examples, frequency, collocations
use: German–German dictionary with real example sentences. From week 5, check how a word is really used before you learn it.
tip: All in German, so it gets easier as you go.

name: Forvo German
what: Native-speaker recordings of single words
use: Hear any word said by native speakers. Use it in the Sounds block when your phone has no German voice.
note: Optional for German because browser de-DE TTS voices are good (D8); use Forvo when you want a human model or a regional variant.
tip: Free; recording your own words needs an account.

name: Most common German words (list)
what: Subtitle-derived German word frequency list, 50,000 forms
use: A plain list of the most frequent German words, from film subtitles. From week 9, use it to check whether a new word is common enough to learn now.
note: Raw text file (word, count per line); the GitHub folder view github.com/hermitdave/FrequencyWords/tree/master/content/2018/de was not fetchable from this session (robots/403), the raw file was. Lemmatise by hand: ich/mich/mir are separate lines.
tip: It opens as a raw text file (word and count on each line).

name: Easy readers (Klett)
what: Paid A1–B1 graded readers, many with audio
use: Short books written for learners, sorted by level. Around week 5 buy one A1 reader and read 10 minutes a day; A2 later.
note: Page shows 87 A1 titles with a level filter (A2: 167, B1: 101). Hueber Lesehefte / Lese-Novelas are the equivalent Hueber series, but shop.hueber.de refuses automated fetches so no Hueber listing URL is given. Price range is typical, not read from the page.
tip: Many titles come with audio.

name: Menschen coursebook (Hueber)
what: Paid mainstream DaF coursebook series, A1–B1, with audio
use: Only if you want a printed coursebook as well. Nicos Weg and FSI already cover the same ground for free.
note: Netzwerk neu (Klett) is the equivalent alternative; only Klett component pages (Intensivtrainer, Grammatik) were reachable, so no Netzwerk series URL is given.
tip: Netzwerk neu (Klett) is the equivalent alternative.

name: FSI Hungarian Basic Course
what: Public-domain drill course: 24 units, PDFs, tapes, graded reader
use: Free US-government course: book (PDF) and audio.
note: The page itself holds the downloads (Volume 1–2 student texts, Unit 01A–24D MP3s, FSI Hungarian Graded Reader with 24 audio selections, and a full ZIP). The tapes are the only native audio at learner tempo.

useByStage.1: From Hungarian week 3: Unit 1 dialogue — pause after each line and say it out loud; then say the drill answers before the speaker. Units 1–2 in weeks 3–4.
useByStage.2: Units 3–5 in weeks 5–8: dialogue first, then the drills out loud.
useByStage.3: Units 6–8 in weeks 9–12; shadow the dialogue speaker.

tip: From the 1960s, so some words are dated, but the structure drills are excellent.

name: HungarianPod101
what: Audio/video lessons with dialogue breakdowns; free tier
use: Short audio lessons with English explanations. One Absolute Beginner lesson a day: listen, then repeat the dialogue line by line.
note: Free lifetime account: first 3 lessons of every series plus 3–5 new free lessons a week; line-by-line transcripts and lesson notes are Premium. Pricing page listed Basic $4, Premium $10, Premium PLUS $23 per month at full price (sale prices lower).
tip: A free account gives the first lessons of every series; the rest is paid.

name: HungarianReference.com
what: Free English-language Hungarian grammar reference
use: Clear English explanations of Hungarian.

useByStage.0: Weeks 1–2: read the pronunciation pages (vowels, consonants, stress) while you do the Sounds block.
useByStage.1: Look a grammar point up only after a drill keeps missing it.

name: MagyarOK coursebook
what: Coursebook A1–B2; site has free audio, worksheets, sample chapter
use: Modern Hungarian coursebook; its site has free audio and sample chapters. Optional from week 5.
note: Neither mnyi.eu nor magyar-ok.hu could be fetched from this session (permission gate on new hosts). University of Pécs announced the site is moving from magyar-ok.hu to mnyi.eu with both live during a transition; if mnyi.eu does not resolve, try https://www.magyar-ok.hu.

name: M1 Híradó (TV news)
what: Public TV news bulletins on demand, Hungarian only
use: Hungarian TV news. From week 9, play the first 2 minutes without text and note place names, numbers and who did what.
note: The topic page returned a server error to the fetcher; a single Híradó video page on mediaklikk.hu did load, confirming bulletins are hosted there. Context: MTVA news went dark 7 Jul 2026 and the Híradó relaunched 20 Aug 2026 with two daily bulletins; hirado.hu currently shows only a 'service under review' notice. The site has an 18+ age gate.

name: Kossuth Rádió
what: Public radio live stream and programme archive
use: Hungarian public radio. One short news item for gisting; speak along with the newsreader for 30 seconds.
note: Relaunched 24 Aug 2026 after the public-media shutdown; the page shows an 'élő' (live) label and programme links behind an 18+ age gate.

name: Telex (news site)
what: Independent Hungarian news site with video
use: Hungarian news site. From week 5, skim the headlines for place names, numbers and dates; full articles only after month 3.
note: The homepage refused the automated fetch (client error, likely a bot wall); individual Telex articles and the English edition https://telex.hu/english loaded fine, so the domain is live.

name: Common Voice (Hungarian)
what: Thousands of short native clips with text; listen in browser
use: Real people reading short sentences. Open Listen, play a clip, then say the sentence yourself. Ten a day.
note: Page loaded (Common Voice app; /hu is the Hungarian locale) but it is a JavaScript app, so clip content could not be inspected by the fetcher. Bulk dataset download has moved to Mozilla Data Collective: https://datacollective.mozillafoundation.org/datasets/cmj8u3p8900bhnxxb50f37mkm (Scripted Speech 24.0 – Hungarian; redirects to mozilladatacollective.com, which could not be fetched).
tip: Volunteer recordings: quality varies, so skip the bad ones.

useByStage.0: Weeks 1–2: open Listen and play a clip while reading its sentence, then say the sentence yourself. Ten a day; copy the sounds, don’t worry about meaning yet.
useByStage.1: Play ten clips while reading the sentence, then say each one yourself, half a second behind the speaker.

name: Tatoeba (Hungarian audio)
what: About 6,900 Hungarian sentences with native audio and translations
use: Short recorded sentences. Pick five, repeat each three times, then write them from memory and check.
note: Page lists 6,914 Hungarian recordings (1,000 most recent shown). For sentences with English translations use Advanced search with from=hun, to=eng, has audio=yes.
tip: Click a sentence to see its English translation.

name: SZTAKI dictionary
what: Standard free Hungarian–English dictionary
use: The standard Hungarian–English dictionary. Write every new noun down with one ending you know (ház, házban), not as a bare word.
note: The site returned a client error to the automated fetcher (likely bot protection); the address is the long-standing one and is cited by Hungarian press as the main free online dictionary.

name: Wiktionary – Hungarian entries
what: 31,000+ Hungarian lemmas with full declension and conjugation tables
use: After a drill miss on an ending, open the word’s entry and read its table of forms once, then drill it again.
note: Many entries carry audio; the tables show stem alternations (kéz → kezet) which the Deconstructor module relies on.
tip: Many entries have audio.

name: Most common Hungarian words (list)
what: Subtitle-derived Hungarian word frequency list, 50,000 forms
use: A plain list of the most frequent Hungarian words (word forms, not dictionary forms). From week 9, use it to check whether a word is common.
note: Raw text file (word, count per line). The GitHub folder view was not fetchable from this session; the raw file was. Inflected forms (házat, házban) appear as separate lines.
tip: Opens as a raw text file.

name: ECL Hungarian sample exams
what: Free ECL sample papers, Hungarian as a foreign language A2–C1
use: Sample papers for a recognised Hungarian exam. Optional, from month 10, as an outside check next to the tutor-run mock interview.
note: The sample-test page could not be fetched (permission gate); its URL is quoted by eduline.hu articles from 2015 and 2025. The ECL 'Magyar mint idegen nyelv' exam page https://ecl.hu/?p=7662 did load and confirms A2/B1/B2/C1 levels.

name: Forvo Hungarian
what: Native-speaker recordings of single Hungarian words
use: Hear any Hungarian word said by native speakers. Use it in the Sounds block, and say your family’s names and towns the same way.
note: Core for Hungarian because browser hu-HU TTS voices are patchy (D8). Request a recording if a family place name is missing.
tip: Phone voices for Hungarian are often missing or poor, so this is your main pronunciation model.

name: italki (tutors)
what: Tutor marketplace; community tutors, pay per lesson
use: Paid online tutors. Book the same tutor for 30 minutes a week (German from week 5; Hungarian from its week 9), send your scenario card ahead and spend the call being questioned about your story.
note: Listings seen: German community tutors from about $5–15 per trial, Hungarian tutors $15–25 per hour (59 available). Marked optional because it costs money; the doctrine's minimum dose is 30 min/week per language.
tip: Community tutors are usually cheaper than professional teachers; try two or three trial lessons before committing.

name: Preply (tutors)
what: Tutor marketplace, alternative to italki
use: Alternative to italki if you can’t find a tutor you like there; same 30-minute weekly format.
cost: pay per lesson (tutor sets the price)

name: Tandem (language exchange)
what: Language-exchange app: text, voice notes, calls
use: Free language-exchange app. From month 3, one 20-minute voice call a week, half in each language.

name: HelloTalk (language exchange)
what: Language-exchange app with corrections and voice rooms
use: Language-exchange app. From month 3, post one short text a week and let native speakers correct it.

name: Claude (chat)
what: Cross-examiner, writing corrector, and drill-item generator
use: Your tutor between sessions.
note: Not a web page to fetch: this is the chat you are already in. Cross-examination starts German week 3 and Hungarian week 10 per D8; the linguistic-console-sessions skill holds the session formats.

useByStage.1: Stuck on a drill? Paste the cue and the answer and ask why it is built that way, or ask for five more example sentences at your level.
useByStage.2: Once a week: Legend → Export for chat, paste it here and get questioned about your story for 15 minutes. Keep asking “why” about drill answers you don’t understand.
useByStage.3: Weekly legend questioning as before; once a month paste a paragraph you wrote and ask for corrections with a one-line reason for each.

tip: Open the Claude app or claude.ai in a new chat. For Hungarian, ask it to use the formal Ön form, like the consulate will.
